Tracing the causal chain: some shoppers' account page requests failed, and digging into why, I find that replicas on the old revision threw a ValueError when reading a summary cache entry of '2400/8' because it wasn't formatted as a valid figure in cents.

Checking whether the logs identify which replica raised it, I piece together from D1 that the new revision's summary_entry_in catches ValueError and returns None instead of raising, so the error text "is not a figure in cents" must come from the old reader's expectation of a bare cents value. This makes me reasonably confident the failing reader belongs to the 5470c1a revision rather than the new one.

For the entry format itself, revision 696c33a changed entries to an amount/items structure per D1's `_ENTRY_FORMAT`, which explains why cache values like "2400/8" show up — they match that new format, not cents. Since P2's rollout at 13:57 left old and new revisions sharing the same cache mid-rollout (T10 shows a split of replicas), the timing lines up: errors started right as P2 deployed, so I can trace the chain from account page failures back to that format change and rollout window, ruling out the earlier P1 deploy as the cause.

I'm checking whether P1 is ruled out by the healthy metrics window (T5, T6) covering from before P1's deploy through onset, with baseline error rates and healthy account page renders confirmed up to 13:56 — no flag changes either (T16), so P1 looks clean. C2, the possibility that the new revision's code itself is simply buggy, isn't actually refuted by anything in the record, even though rollback confirmation doesn't distinguish between C1 and C2 — so I'm leaving that open rather than ruling it out.

Now I need to work out why the old revision would encounter new-format entries in the first place.

The rollout apparently stalled partway: T10 shows three replicas still running the old revision and three on the new one, with the rolling update paused — and all six share the same cache under the same key. I'm noting that F1's claim about entries landing under the bare shopper id is an untested reading, and D1 doesn't actually show whether the cache key changed. So the likely root cause is that the new revision switched the cache entry format (from a bare cents number to an 'amount/items' string) while writing to the same shared cache key the old revision still reads from.

Old-revision replicas, still live during the paused rollout, pull these new-format entries and can't parse them, raising rather than falling back gracefully — which matches the error in G3714. The reasoning chain for this ties the format change to D1, the shared-key assumption to F1, the mixed rollout state to T10, and the actual failure to G3714, though I notice the shared-key claim rests only on F1 without corroborating data.

Tracing who actually wrote "2400/8" into the shared cache — D1 shows the new format, and the old reader's failure (raising rather than falling back) seems explained by D1's behavior alone, not F1. So the root cause claim likely rests on D rows, not an unsupported F row, making the statement false.

Actually, maybe not a separate contributing factor—it's really the same mechanism as the version skew. But I notice the old module's docstring claims "nothing here fails a page," yet the ValueError does exactly that for malformed entries—so the fallback logic was incomplete, only covering misses and unreachable cache, not malformed data. That gap in the fallback coverage could itself be worth flagging as a contributing factor distinct from the rolling-update timing issue.

Beyond that, I'm noting a second contributing factor: there was no compatibility check between cache-format revisions before deploying the change—nothing verified that the still-running old reader could parse the new writer's entries. Adding a CI check that runs the previous revision's reader against the new writer's output would have caught this before release. A third factor is that no one was paged despite the alert firing, though Argus auto-mitigated, so I'm weighing whether human intervention would have shortened the incident.

The rollout stayed paused in a mixed state with 6 replicas instead of 3, and nothing rolled it back automatically — only Argus's manual rollback ended the rising error rate that started at 13:57. That's another contributing factor worth flagging, with an action item to add an automatic error-rate rollback gate to io-shop's deployment process.

On the cache reader issue, I notice the new revision already fixes this — its reader returns None for unreadable entries instead of failing, so the gap only exists in the old revision that got rolled back into place. So the real action item is adding a regression test confirming the cache reader treats unreadable entries as a miss, since that behavior is already patched but needs verification.

For CF-2, I'll add a pre-merge check that runs the production reader against entries the new revision writes, plus a process requirement that cache format changes use a new key or version rather than reusing the one the running revision reads — keeping it to one prevent action and one process action. For CF-3, I'll gate io-shop's rolling update on error rate so it halts and rolls back automatically, and separately look into why the rollout process itself allowed this.

I also want to consider why the rollout paused halfway with 6 replicas on a deployment sized for 3, leaving mixed revisions serving with nothing flagging it — that seems like a reasonable detect item: alerting when an io-shop rollout stays paused with two revisions still serving traffic, though I want to avoid duplicating something already covered by the mixed-state chain step.

For "went well," I'm noting the Investigator correctly identified the split replica state across revisions (T10), Argus and the Mitigation Agent rolled back and confirmed the fix (T19, T22), Argus checked flag history and found no changes (T16), and Code-Fix appropriately declined to keep a fix that wouldn't help on its own (T24).

For what went wrong, I'm flagging that nobody was paged despite the incident, though the AI-3 automatic sync being off was working as designed rather than a failure. The Investigator's comparison between C1 and C2 looks fine, and I don't see anything else to flag.

On "got lucky," I'm being careful here — the new revision's reader treating unreadable text as a miss (D1) was deliberate design, not luck, and the error only affecting requests hitting an old replica with new-format entries was a consequence of that design rather than chance. I'll leave this section empty since nothing here was actually luck.

For what's still at risk, I'm thinking through whether entries written under a key the old revision reads could still be cached there, potentially causing the old revision to fail on account pages, and whether rolling forward again would just repeat the same issue.

Metrics show things returned to normal at 14:05, and the risk is clear: rolling revision 696c33a back out as-is could cause account pages to fail again as long as older-revision replicas run alongside it. For ruling things out, P1 gets eliminated by the T5/T6 metrics showing onset at 13:57, since Gad41 was rendering normally from 13:35–13:56, which postdates P1. Flag changes are also ruled out since T16 shows zero flag changes by anyone other than Argus during that hour, and flags were read back clean.

I'm noting the dates for P2 and the T10 state, and working through the assumption that the '2400/8' entries came from replicas of revision 696c33a, inferred from the format in D1, with the writer being outside the repository per F1.

I need to phrase the plain-language cause carefully: a new version started saving a stored shortcut for account pages in a new layout while some servers still ran the old version, which couldn't read that layout and failed instead of recomputing it. I'm being careful with wording here since words like "half" or "a third" are banned for stating quantities not explicitly in the record, so I'll use "some servers" instead. I'm also flagging that the claim about the writer being outside the repo is only supported at a "likely" confidence level based on F1.

Now I'm building the causal chain step by step: first citing G3714, Gbac1, and AL1 to establish that account page requests failed from the start with a cache-read error, matching the shop's own warning about rising error rates. Then I'm tying the failure to the reader encountering an entry like '{G3714.1}' and raising a ValueError since it wasn't a valid cents figure, citing Gc956 and G3714 — though I need to double check that "instead of falling back" phrasing stays within what the record supports.

For the next step, I need to be careful not to write literal braces like '{amount_cents}/{items_counted}' since those could be mistaken for figure references — better to describe it as "amount and purchase count separated by a slash" when explaining that revision 696c33a (deployed at P2) changed the cache entry format, which matches when the cache errors began, citing P2, D1, and Gc956, while treating this as ruled out as the root cause itself.

For the next step, I'm working out that some replicas (T10.2 of T10.3) ran the new revision 696c33a while others (T10.5) still ran the old 5470c1a during a paused rolling update, meaning both versions were reading the same cache simultaneously — since 696c33a's own reader skips over the new text format, the reader actually throwing errors must belong to 5470c1a, which still expects a bare cents figure, citing T10, D1, and G3714.

Now I'm sequencing the explanation: first the new entry format, then why an old reader encountered it, and finally the single-sentence root cause — that the service broke because the revision still running alongside the new one reads the same cache but can't parse the new format.

I'm also confirming the chain reaches an actual cause rather than resting on unverified assumptions, checking which contributing factors (missing compatibility checks, no reader fallback, no automatic rollback) are already addressed elsewhere versus need to be captured as my own action items, and making sure I avoid citing specific figures when writing the final response.

I've submitted the postmortem for the io-shop HighErrorRate incident.

- **Cause:** Revision 696c33a, deployed at {P2.1}, changed summary cache entries from a bare cents figure to amount and purchase count joined by a slash. At {T10.1}, {T10.2} of {T10.3} replicas ran the new revision and {T10.5} still ran 5470c1a, with the rolling update paused. The older revision read the new entries, couldn't parse them, and failed account pages instead of working the figure out again.
- **Unverified parts:** I marked the cause as not resting on an unrun reading. The diff (D1) shows the new format, and the logs show the failing reader meeting '{G3714.1}'. Two things are still inferred, and I listed both as assumptions:
  - The failing reader was 5470c1a's. The logs don't say which revision raised the error; the inference is that 696c33a's own reader skips text it can't read.
  - Replicas of 696c33a wrote the entries. Code-Fix's reading says the code that writes them is outside the repository, and nothing ran to show it.
- **Ruled out:** the earlier deploy P1, by the metrics read across the hours after it and by normal account-page logs right up to the onset. Flags too: the history showed no changes.
- **Still at risk:** rolling 696c33a out again as it stands could fail account pages again while replicas of the older revision still run beside it.

**Contributing factors** (none is answered by the record's own items, so each has a new item):
1. **The older reader had no fallback for unreadable entries.** Its fallback covers a cache miss and a cache that can't be reached, but not an entry it can't read. New item: add a test that requires the page to render from its fallback when it meets an unfamiliar entry.
2. **No compatibility check was seen.** Nothing showed a check that the revision already running could read what the new one writes. New items: a pre-merge check that runs the production revision's reader against the new writer's output, and a review rule that a changed entry format goes under a new key.
3. **No automatic rollback was seen.** Nothing rolled the rollout back when errors rose; only Argus's rollback ended it. New item: gate io-shop's rolling update on error rate so it halts and rolls back on its own.

**Other new items and lessons:**
- I put "nobody was paged" under what went wrong, with an item to page on-call for this alert. It isn't tied to a contributing factor, since a page wouldn't clearly have shortened this incident.
- Two new items don't overlap with AI-1 to AI-3, all of which I left as they were:
  - Find out why the rollout paused with {T10.3} replicas on a deployment sized for {T10.6}.
  - Clear or check entries in the new format still in the cache before moving forward again.
- I left "got lucky" empty because nothing in the record shows chance helping.
